pages.name: About This Journal
pages.html:
Ispin's second route, as the Crows have actually travelled it: Vogler to the Vingard, the dwarf-road down to Maelgoth, the ambush country beyond, and the river running south toward the forest.

Arc II describes this journey as three interchangeable route thresholds. That is the right level of abstraction for a book and the wrong one for a table that is on the water this week, so these pages record the specific places instead. Each one has a scene with its map, its pins and its player handouts, and the scenes chain in travel order.

Where the company stands

Four at the table: Solanthis Brightweave (exhausted, bound to Kelrar), Clipper Nautilus (wounded, keeping the crow), Darrow Bonecrusher, and Fizzwick Blunderbottom (unconscious at 0 hit points). Level 3, advancing to 4 when the wyvern is settled. The camp is The Vingard · South Bank, and the fight there is unresolved.

Three Crows are elsewhere: Alice, Sylas and Jinx, carrying Kattal go-Zemu home to the Isles of the Minotaurs. Nothing on these pages assumes their return.

DM Note — what these pages are not

These are location notes, not session plans. They carry no tracker guidance and no arc structure, because the arc journals already hold that and this journey is being played out of order relative to them. Where a location has already been played, the page records what happened so the map can be reused; where it has not, the page says what is there and leaves the rest to the table.

pages.name: Funeral Reach
pages.html:
The slow water below Vogler, where Ispin's boat was burned and set adrift.

Wide and shallow, with gravel bars that stand clear in summer. The Vingard runs west to east here and the current is gentle enough to work a boat against. Both banks are grazed down to turf.

The launching

The company carried the coffin down from the village and set the boat alight from the southern bank. It drifted perhaps two hundred yards before it went under. Anyone who wants to find the spot again can: there is a cut willow on the bank where the stretcher was rested.

The bar where the crows gathered

Birds came down onto the gravel bar while the boat burned, and stayed after. In hindsight this is the first of them. At the time it was just birds.

Using it again

A quiet map. Good for a return, a burial, a conversation on the water, or a crossing under pressure if the company comes back this way with something behind them.

pages.name: The Open Crossing
pages.html:
Solamnic plain between the river and the dwarf-road. A mile of nothing in every direction.

Grass, scrub, outcrops of grey rock, and a line of standing stones nobody local can date. The road is a wheel-rut rather than a built road. This is where the carriage came apart.

The standing stones

Five of them, in a rough line running north-east. Pre-Cataclysm, by the weathering. They are the only cover on the map and everyone fighting here will end up using them.

What it is for

Open-field encounters where neither side can hide: cavalry, fliers, a ranged exchange, or a conversation that cannot be overheard. Weather matters more here than anywhere else on the route.

pages.name: The Defile
pages.html:
The pass carrying the dwarf-road down toward Maelgoth.

A winding floor of broken rock with walls of boulder and scree on both sides. Perhaps forty feet across at the narrow. The high ground on either flank is climbable with effort and commands the whole length.

Ambush country

Everyone who uses this road knows what it is, which means a competent ambush here is laid by someone who expects to be expected. Traffic travels it in groups and in daylight.

DM Note

The map is drawn so the pass bends twice: a party cannot see end to end, and neither can anything waiting for them. Use the bends rather than a surprise roll.

pages.name: Maelgoth
pages.html:
The outer hall of the underground dwarven city. Forge-channel down the middle, trade stalls along both walls.

Visitors get this far and generally no further. It is warm, loud, and busy at all hours, because the forge channel never goes out and the shifts never stop. The air tastes of hot metal.

The commission

The folding boat was built here, to Kattal's design with Solanthis's enchantments laid in afterwards. The boatwrights are still here and would remember the work, which matters if it needs repair — it has already been damaged once.

The lizards, and Nigel

Alice, Sylas and Clipper recovered the missing giant lizards from the lower stalls. The honey badger attached itself during the same errand and nobody has successfully explained how.

DM Note — the black-robed stranger

Sylas's encounter happened in the deeper levels, not this hall. The master who intervened, sealed the intrusion and examined his memories has not been identified to the players. Keep that unidentified for now; the Tower is the place to answer it.

pages.name: The Toll Station
pages.html:
A bar across the road, a hut behind it, and a family locked in the back.

The toll is a real one and was being collected legitimately until recently. The people collecting it now are not the people appointed to, and the difference is visible to anyone who looks at the ledger.

The captives

A local family, held in the rear room since the station changed hands. They are the reason the arrangement has held: the road's regular users assume the family is still running it.

What the ledger shows

Takings, dated, and a second column that does not correspond to traffic. Money is going somewhere other than the road authority, and the pattern of it matches what was found at House Bakaris.

DM Note

This is a thread into the wider conspiracy rather than a roadside encounter. The second column is the evidence; the brigands themselves do not know who they are paying.

pages.name: The Ambush
pages.html:
Where the elves and the red-robed mage came back. Kattal died on this ground.

Open camp, three fires, no cover worth the name. The map is deliberately exposed: the Fireball that opened the attack did what it did because there was nowhere to be.

What happened

Alice sold powdered unicorn horn to the visitors. They left, argued among themselves, and returned. The opening was a Fireball and coordinated missile fire, and most of the company went down in the first exchange. Solanthis accepted Kelrar's offer to survive it. Kattal did not survive it.

Using it again

Returning here is a strong scene and the map is kept for that reason. The ground still shows the burn.

DM Note — the red-robed mage

Unaccounted for. Solanthis has stated an intention to find him. Whether he was a renegade, a sanctioned Red Robe acting privately, or something arranged by a third party is still open, and the Conclave in Arc I is the natural place to start closing it.

pages.name: The Scarecrow Fields
pages.html:
A farmer, a crop, and too many crows. The company is named for this going badly once already.

Four fields in strips with hedgerows between them, a track across the middle, and a barn at the north-east corner. Four scarecrows, none of them effective.

Standing in the field

Solanthis and Clipper spent an afternoon pretending to be scarecrows here, which is exactly what the original Crows did and exactly as unsuccessful. It is the scene where the two of them stopped being angry with each other.

The crow that stayed

Clipper's crow joined the company on this map. It has since started attracting others.

DM Note

Keep this map light. It earns its place as the counterweight to the ambush two scenes earlier, and the Habbakuk thread begins here in retrospect rather than announcing itself.

pages.name: The Mudflats
pages.html:
Reed beds, standing water, and mud that holds what it catches.

Islands of firm ground in a field of shallow water, with a bank of dry land along the southern edge. Movement off the firm ground is slow and loud.

Sinking

A wild magic surge put Fizzwick waist-deep here, shouting insults he did not choose, which is how Darrow and Fizzwick met the other two.

What was following

The goblins pursuing Darrow and Fizzwick over the raid they survived. Families, not raiders — the raiders were killed, and these are the ones who were spared.

DM Note

The spared goblins are a live thread. They have a legitimate grievance and the party has a defensible reason for what they did. Do not resolve it by making the goblins monsters.

pages.name: The Fishing Platform
pages.html:
A collapsing stage out over the water, with an old knight on the wrong end of it.

The platform runs twenty feet out from the northern bank and the supports under the last third have gone. Nets hang below it, and there were crows caught in them.

Banthar

A retired Knight of Solamnia, fishing where he should not have been, trapped when the stage gave way. He is grateful, embarrassed, and better informed about the war than he first appears.

The blue thread

The crows that led the party here carried a length of blue thread. Solanthis associated it with Habbakuk. The birds offered bread crusts afterwards, which is either gratitude or a god with a sense of humour.

DM Note — the Habbakuk thread

This is the clearest signal so far and it has not been paid off. The god's interest can develop as a sequence of tests about compassion, trust and belonging, and the natural payoff is recognising Darrow and Fizzwick as Crows rather than passengers.

pages.name: The Broken Aqueduct
pages.html:
A Solamnic water-channel with two spans fallen in, and darkness inside that is not entirely natural.

The channel is a stone trough roughly thirty feet wide with walls to either side. Two breaches open onto a long drop. Inside, line of sight is short and sound carries badly.

Darkness, and what is in it

Darkmantles. They do not need to make their own darkness in here, which makes them considerably worse. Solanthis was suffocated and dropped during the fight.

Harmony

A dragonborn woman found trapped among them. She supplied the mushroom that revived Solanthis and offered to take the company to a campsite. They declined, on the grounds that she had said very little about herself.

DM Note

Harmony is unresolved and the party's suspicion is reasonable. She can return as an ally, a rival salvager, or something with an interest in the Tower; nothing so far commits her either way.

pages.name: South Bank
pages.html:
Where the Crows are now. Night camp on the southern bank, the folding boat drawn up, and a wyvern coming out of the cloud.

Shingle landing, scrub and driftwood above the waterline, treeline at the back of the map. One fire. The water is on the northern edge and the boat is at the landing.

It comes out of the cloud

The same wyvern the original Crows met on the road out of Vogler, still carrying Kingfisher Festival decorations and considerably more scarred. Fizzwick opened with a Chaos Bolt and took its attention.

Where the fight stands

Fizzwick is unconscious at 0 hit points. Clipper is wounded. Solanthis is exhausted and has already refused Kelrar once while dying. Darrow is holding the line. The wyvern is alive and the outcome is open.

DM Note — the wyvern

It is wounded and has been for a long time. It is not hunting the party specifically; it is hunting because it is injured and hungry, and it recognises them. There is a version of this where it can be driven off or even helped, and a version where it kills someone. Both are honest.

DM Note — Kelrar

The demon will offer again if Solanthis drops. He refused at the aqueduct, which cost him nothing he can see yet. A second refusal while a companion is dying is a different question.

pages.name: The Run South
pages.html:
Open river below the camp, running toward the forest country.

Deeper and faster than the Funeral Reach. Boulders stand in the channel and there is no bank worth landing on for most of its length. This is a boat map: the folding boat is the floor.

Running it

Treat the channel as the battlefield and the boat as moving terrain. A creature in the water is going downstream whether it likes it or not.

What it connects

South Bank to the Waystation, and from there Riverlanding and the road into the forest. If the company wants to make time rather than distance, this is where they do it.

pages.name: The Waystation
pages.html:
A river inn on the south road: one long room, a hearth, and whoever else is going the same way.

Rough but warm. Beds upstairs, a stable nobody uses, and a landlord who asks nothing and remembers everything.

The other travellers

Always three or four parties in the room: carters, a militia patrol off duty, refugees moving north, occasionally somebody who should not be this far from a city. Good place to put a rumour, a recruiter, or someone looking for the Crows.

DM Note

This is the map for a long rest with consequences. Nothing has to happen here; something usually should.

pages.name: Riverlanding
pages.html:
The last town of any size before the forest country.

A wharf, a market square, a militia post and perhaps three hundred people. Cargo moves through here and so does everything else.

The militia question

They have started asking travellers where they are going and writing the answers down. It is new, it is not local policy, and the sergeant doing it is uncomfortable about it.

The road to the forest

South out of the market square. Beyond Riverlanding the road stops being maintained, which is as close as the map gets to a warning.

DM Note

This is the hand-off into Arc I's forest material. The scene chains to The Forest of Wayreth, and the Crows arrive at the Tower from here.
